summary: A reading of stories and ads from American men's adventure magazines of the 1950s and 1960s, pulp publications for postwar men that mixed soft-core porn, racist caricature, sexualised minors and insecure fantasies of masculinity.

evidence.note: genre said to begin after WWII, peak in late 1950s-60s, gone by the 1970s
illustrator's son on the audience: servicemen who never saw combat and doubted their manhood
first magazine read is an April 1960 issue of Climax
segment on greasers and switchblades as a moral panic of the era
magazines treat sex with sixteen-year-olds as normal; a reader photo appears to show a minor
second magazine is a 1957 issue of Courage, with quack vitamin and correspondence-course ads
harem story prompts real history of the Red Sea slave trade into Saudi Arabia, abolished 1962
Kashmir story in Exotic Adventures sexualises a trafficked teenage girl
vivid reading of a woman being killed by crabs
last magazine read is a December 1969 issue of Man's Combat
Man's Combat story built on SS men raping nuns, loosely drawn from the Nowogrodek martyrs

notes: Primary theme misogyny-manosphere stands in for postwar toxic masculinity; no vocabulary entry for pulp or print culture. Covered span is the issues read (1957-1969) plus the genre's postwar start; the 1920s-1962 Saudi slave-trade history is treated as background to one article, though SA is kept in the setting. Settings of the fictional stories (Kashmir, Belize, Tangier, France) are left out.
